text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Multiple specific details from article (half million miles without crash, alert system for driveways, vibrating seats, steering/acceleration/braking capabilities)", "quality": "Use of concrete textual evidence", "description": "Essay B grounds its argument in specific, verifiable details from the source article rather than making unsupported claims."}, {"evidence": "Clear topic sentences and paragraph organization around distinct benefits (safety, convenience, accident reduction)", "quality": "Logical organization", "description": "Essay B structures its argument with separate paragraphs developing distinct points, whereas Essay A jumps between related but undeveloped ideas."}, {"evidence": "Addresses counterargument about accidents by acknowledging small risk percentage while arguing benefits outweigh concerns", "quality": "Engagement with complexity", "description": "Essay B acknowledges potential objections rather than ignoring them, showing more sophisticated argumentative thinking."}, {"evidence": "Consistent focus on why driverless cars should be developed, with each paragraph supporting the main position", "quality": "Argument coherence", "description": "Essay B maintains a clear through-line connecting evidence to its central claim, while Essay A's points feel disconnected and sometimes contradictory."}, {"evidence": "Rhetorical questions and direct address to reader ('Have you ever thought...', 'What if you have an incoming phone call')", "quality": "Engagement with audience", "description": "Essay B uses rhetorical devices to connect with the reader and make the argument more persuasive, while Essay A remains more detached."}]}
